### Guarded counted loops over primitive arrays

Source `a5e5f50bb45a820935591a828d90b82ed321f743` extends the experimental
compiler with a bounded, application-independent proof for signed increasing
counted loops. It supports captured primitive arrays, float/double/long and
narrow stores, affine indices (including reversed and strided accesses), and
already-cached nonvolatile static arrays. There is no application opt-in.
Calls, callbacks, allocations, internal cycles, unproved counter updates and
additional loop exits retain the ordinary path. This first version deliberately
does not treat a Math import as a callback-free operation.

The guard proves mathematical index endpoints, physical memory coverage,
metadata generations, remaining trip count and sufficient fuel. If metadata is
missing, an ordinary iteration runs and its original backedge retries the guard;
there are no speculative getters or replayed guest effects. A successful version
charges exactly the original header-poll count. The structurer sometimes places
an entire continuation on a loop's exit arm: the implementation extracts that
continuation once, avoiding duplicate following loops, calls or writes.
Temporary plans are released. Candidate discovery and extra emitted bytes have
fixed bounds; loops with more removable memory guards are considered first.

The initial `70af609` version selects six decoder loops and matches every byte of
the largest HotSpot Vorbis sample. Its 243.299 ms sample timing is not evidence
of a gain. The final version changes prioritization, literal handling and code
accounting, so that observation is not relabeled as the final revision.

#### Unchecked memory-cost diagnostics

`apps/loading/unchecked-memory-probe.cjs` is an explicitly unsafe Node-only
causal diagnostic, not imported by a launcher. It temporarily changes compiler
emission in the exact archived source, restores the loader hook afterwards,
marks the resulting observation instrumented, and appends only to the existing
`benchmark.json`. It records source/harness/hook hashes, assumptions, compile-site

#### Proved outer-loop resumption experiment

The corrected source is java-tools commit
`ad82ae4915cd69f90265867fb0e49114794fd6ef`, retained on
`experiment/teavm-native-parity` through `eece78a17b580c41b0860459cca4cd653fa5bf7b`.
The branch also preserves the two measured intermediate source revisions. Master
and the selected runtime artifact remain `cbcf8ad`; this experiment is **not a
full-loading improvement or deployment**.

`src/jit/structuredLoopResume.js` proves one outer-loop entry automatically,
without an application flag or game identity. The header must have an original
Java PC and an empty operand stack, and be reachable through only sequence/block
wrappers. No resumed successor may enter the skipped prefix. Every needed SSA
input must be reconstructed from a typed, live Java frame slot or a total
literal. Existing protected boolean-capture metadata is also restored, even
when ordinary Java liveness no longer needs it. Unusable verifier slots,
including wide-value second words, are omitted exactly as in the spill path.
Exception regions, conditional-arm entries, irreducible copies, guarded nested
kernels and GC argument/result transports retain their existing entry protocol.
Canonical nested-callee ownership remains a separate restriction.

The existing native loop body is shared; only its prefix is skipped at the
proved resume entry. Entry-only copying, clearing and ownership transfers are
not replayed. A weak frame marker is set **only by a real fuel exit**. The
scheduler preserves the empty header stack and yields before executing another
canonical bytecode, then prioritizes the proved entry. Readiness-guard failures
do not set this marker, so they can advance through canonical initialization
instead of spinning at the header. The five-million execution budget is
unchanged. Runtime restore callbacks capture scalar slot/type metadata; the
SSA plan is released with the other compiler analyses.

The first PC-only prototype (`d0469a0`) was superseded by an actual-fuel marker
and a mid-resume readiness-invalidation regression. The next prototype
(`d2e6bcd`) was superseded by preserving protected captured state across every
subsequent spill. Those observations remain in the one canonical report.

that their combination is fast; do not add these independent timings together
to attribute the full decoder's cost.

A small prototype combined the representation and bounds predicates into one
native fast-path branch, preserving separate native exceptions and checked
foreign/null fallbacks. Source `cb4c00abb2e4dcdd19bf20b1374d87221bb91eef`
passes **152/152** heap-array/array-ABI assertions, but regresses the loads-only
case to **26.278 ms** and the no-readback butterfly to **34.430 ms**. Restoring

withdrawn; `598634f5c7207bb28555408822353660feef2601` has exactly the retained
`471defcc` source tree. No full-loading comparison was spent on this regression.

The emitted TeaVM Wasm uses typed GC arrays and ordinary arithmetic; it does not
remove the butterfly's output readback. Our emitted Wasm has separate heap
representation and bounds paths. The rejected branch experiment shows that
simply combining those predicates is not a demonstrated improvement.

The harness also now copies four **unchanged** original fixture classes for one
small real decoder case: `Bzip2Decoder`, `Bzip2DecoderState`,
`UsernameResponseSupport` and its verification dependency
`ContextualRuntimeException`. Each class hash must match the pinned full-loading
inventory, and TeaVM must consume those same class bytes. The input is the
recorded `0-27.bin` archive: 1,649 packed bytes and 10,750 output bytes.
Each process decodes it **once**, with no repetitions or decoder warmup. Inputs,
the decoder-state class initializer and output allocation precede timing;
the output checksum follows it.

An explicit diagnostic control reads the transform-table holder's ordinary
static integer before timing. It initializes only that holder class, with no
archive decoding. In three fresh pairs, the ordinary case takes **348.751 ms JVM
versus 0.411 ms TeaVM**; the initialized-holder control takes **8.644 versus
0.392 ms**. The control changes 10,488 legacy bit-reader entries into native
entries, with zero execution-time Java compilation in both cases. This isolates
a severe cold-initialization continuation penalty. Moving initialization out
of a timer is **not** a runtime fix or loading acceptance result.

A separate instrumented initialized-holder run records **20,336** primitive-array
cast imports. This confirms the previously documented Bzip cast issue; import
counts alone do not assign the remaining time to casts. The new matched integer
load pair changes only an array parameter into an `Object` parameter cast to
`int[]` inside the loop. At one million iterations the JVM takes **1.878 ms**
typed and **29.943 ms** with casts, while TeaVM takes **1.063 ms** in either form.

At eight million iterations a second effect dominates: the original cast loop

### Cold initialization: recovering native execution at a proved checkpoint

A smaller generic case now reproduces the cold archive's continuation failure.
Its initializer records a preceding caller-side prefix increment, followed by
10,000 bit-reader iterations and one tail increment. The benchmark checks the
initializer's observation and every effect count as well as the HotSpot checksum.
The initialized-holder control performs no decoder or loop warmup; its different
initializer observation has its own reference checksum.

All observations below use identical Java fixture source
`0c442c79fe51457bc9d7eaa803f43339d7c8a03f5a43cca8d795984ad3695195`
and the same eight class files in TeaVM and JVM, including the unchanged four
original codec classes. Each cell is a median of three fresh-process pairs.
No guest workload is replayed, and there is zero execution-time Java compilation.

| JVM source | Generic cold loop ms | Cold archive ms | Reason for the next step |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `e81bfff2` control | 88.707 | 338.932 | Native code exists but the cold continuation does not regain it |
| `9e0b0940` | 7.879 | 332.693 | Scalar/baseline JS handoff fixes the ordinary frame, not the canonical child |
| `08b155ce` | — | 334.092 | Per-bytecode tests pass, but production interpreter batches pass the checkpoint |
| `d63902df` | — | 18.181 | Batch boundary fixes the real archive; later full validation exposes repeated handoffs |
| `3732b9b7` | 8.713 | 11.769 | Final bounded handoff, retaining normal native fuel resumption |

For the final source, TeaVM takes **0.029 ms** in the generic cold case and
**0.380 ms** for the archive. The initialized controls take **0.375 ms JVM
versus 0.029 ms TeaVM** for the loop, and **8.171 versus 0.412 ms** for the
archive. The cold archive improves substantially, but these figures still fail
1.10x. Small absolute timings and variation in the archive's ready-owner samples
do not support a claim that its remaining gap has disappeared.

The causal sequence is now explicit:

1. A cold guard materializes the precise child Java Frame. A native caller's
   exit marks that child for canonical interpretation, even if the child's own
   method has no handlers.
2. The completed initializer leaves a valid, fully materialized loop state, but
   the blanket continuation policy prevents native re-entry. In the control,
   the decoder makes 10,488 legacy bit-reader entries.
3. Permitting only the existing proved empty-stack checkpoint is insufficient
   if interpreter batching walks past that point without a JIT probe. The new
   production-loop regression demonstrates this difference from single-tick
   unit execution.
4. Eligible interpreter batches now stop at that boundary after actual bytecode
   progress. Re-entry keeps the exact Java Frame and its canonical ancestry;
   native locals and lazy metadata are reconstructed from that frame. The
   synchronized parent and its handler/monitor obligations keep their existing
   continuation. The final archive run makes all **10,490** bit-reader entries
   through native calls.

This does not enter arbitrary blocks or initialize an untaken class early.
Only an existing complete module with a reconstruction proof, initialized guard
owners, no pending child/exception state, and an empty stack can use the
checkpoint. Owned JS continuations retain their lexical locals. Debugger checks,
denied methods, class initializers, entry-only ownership shapes and the existing
array-result restriction retain their previous paths. No new runtime flag or
game identity is involved.

The first full campaign on `d63902df` passed correctness and AOT checks, but
`validateGraphics` then showed **64 native entries and exits**, versus two in
the control. This validation occurs after the loading timer; omitting it would
hide a real continuation regression. The final source permits one non-fuel
checkpoint attempt per invocation. A further refusal keeps the invocation on
its supported fallback. Genuine native fuel spills retain their explicit
resumption marker; fresh/recycled frame entries and normal returns clear the
attempt bookkeeping. This prevents a new handoff storm without interpreting a
prefix twice.

### Receiver-tree controls and primitive-array class identity

The next reduction retains the scalar-codebook algorithm's data-dependent tree

eight-bit tree and a deterministic input byte stream are prepared before timing.
Each fresh process decodes 100,000 symbols and consumes exactly 100,000 bytes;
there is no stream wrap, reset or decode warmup. The tree is synthetic, so this
is an operation control, not a replacement for the original-sample comparison.

The separate instrumented run verifies 100,000 native `readScalar` entries and
800,000 native bit-reader entries, no inlining and no exits. Thus the intended
call path survives compilation. All three timing variants use fixture source
`543e4ee86984488a993c3070da165c370b73382e7c8885a0f92a06b14c04c9c9`

Code inspection identifies a separate missing type hint: ordinary VM-created

There is no new flag, game identity or preprocessing rule.

At the user's request, stop speculative compiler changes and reduce the
remaining cost first. The runtime stays at retained `592f30f0`. Three added
source controls consume the same stream once, changing one category at a time:
combine the per-symbol calls into one method, cache the tree reference, then
keep the reader array and cursors locally until the end. These are diagnostics
on valid input, not replacements for arbitrary guest programs; moving field
accesses can change observable behavior on exceptional/foreign paths.

The new ten-class fixture source is
`4c9dfc9fbabb177703a3a29d6d6580d142ad4faee1f4512529e0461ef841cb3c`.
All four modes consume one million symbols, assert the exact final byte/bit
cursors, and match fresh HotSpot checksum `-1268584370`. JVM.js and TeaVM consume
identical class files. No guest warmup, replay or timed preparation is added.
Three fresh process pairs per case use the same eager native Wasm flags, one
GiB Node heap limit and CPU 2 as the earlier controls.

| Tree reference cached; reader fields | 86.096 | 72.668 | 1.185x |
| Tree and reader arrays/cursors local | 73.335 | 41.905 | 1.750x |

Each JVM observation has zero guest-time Java compilation. The original mode
records one million native `readScalarInline` entries with zero exits; each

reader state also removes its associated initialization/capability/cache work;
the timing does not isolate the cost of a store instruction alone.

### Boolean arrays: reducing the representation boundary before changing defaults

The byte/boolean control led to a generic native `[Z` capability in java-tools,
kept separate from the signed-byte ABI. It normalizes loads as nonzero-to-true
and stores as `value & 1`. Private allocation ownership, exact view kind and
same unshared memory are required. Null, foreign arrays, custom observable
metadata and unsupported representations retain the checked path. Metadata
caches are invalidated before callbacks that could change those properties.

The first prototype (`47780461`) reduces the boolean parameter-loop median
from **51.155 to 3.391 ms**; the byte control stays approximately 2.24 ms.
However, it makes the original audio sample worse: **113.858 ms** versus the
fresh baseline's **102.087 ms**. The large loop amortizes metadata publication;
the original floor sorter repeatedly enters short methods. The initial
prototype is therefore unsuitable for retention despite its loop-kernel win.

Two new matched controls isolate that difference. Both call a small static
field-array helper with bounded recursion, once per iteration, and assert the
actual native helper-entry count and zero exits after execution. A first
nonrecursive helper was inlined; those earlier observations remain associated
with their own fixture identity and are excluded from this per-call comparison.
There is no flag disabling the normal inliner. All controls still compare
HotSpot checksums, use fresh processes and exclude preparation from timing.

| Cheaper safe validation `cf8f45ff` | 205.149 | 10.152 |
| Share validated field generations `8996cad6` | 78.997 | 10.214 |

These successive changes each address the isolated publication cost. One
8-byte scratch header per VM replaces the Wasm multi-result handoff. Captured
intrinsics inspect canonical views without invoking public diagnostic getters.
Repeated readers of the same cached field generation share validated metadata,
while each captured Java reference retains its own metadata and generation.
Unknown generations on external resume never share: old and fresh references
can differ after suspension. Callback invalidation clears both the private
reader cache and the shared capability. The scratch header adds neither a
per-method retained payload nor a compiler-analysis root.

### Reduce the decoder's actual bit-reading algorithm

The 52-case fixture adds four buffered-reader controls before making another
VM change. They copy the pinned decoder's refill and arithmetic order and use
the original `Bzip2DecoderState` class. HotSpot independently calls the original
private `Bzip2Decoder.readBits` through reflection outside timing, checking both
the result checksum and all four changed state values. Helper, inline-field
and local-state variants must match that oracle. The local version is only a
valid-input reduction; it changes partial state on exceptions and is not a
proposed rewrite of guest code.

Each row has three fresh JVM/TeaVM process pairs, CPU 2, eager native Wasm on
both engines and a one-GiB heap limit. Preparation and input creation precede
timing. There is no warmup or replay. The ready-helper variant constructs only
the otherwise empty helper owner before timing; it never reads any bits and
must report zero caller exits.

| One million requests, median ms | JVM | TeaVM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Helper with cold owner | 27.179 | 3.907 |
| Same helper, initialized owner | 25.822 | 3.743 |
| Same field operations inline | 14.073 | 2.838 |
| Local state | 5.098 | 2.508 |

At 10,000 requests, the cold/ready helper medians are **1.741/0.784 ms** in the
JVM versus **0.037/0.037 ms** in TeaVM. Moving initialization out removes the
first caller exit, but the million-request ready control remains about 6.90x
TeaVM. The local control still takes 2.03x TeaVM. These contrasts separate
first-use effects, helper-boundary overhead and field-state overhead; they do
not uniquely attribute every instruction's cost or prove full-loading gains.

### Measure the native call boundary without changing the JVM

`apps/loading/buffered-call-controls.mjs` generates a small native reader and
caller over the same 490,954 original requests and pinned input. Three forms
share identical reader instructions: a same-module call, an imported Wasm
function and a table call to that native function in another instance. A
fourth table form adds a status/value return and a caller status check. Its
reader arithmetic and field operations are generated from the same source;
only the return protocol differs. Both cross-instance forms share memory with
the caller; the table stores the exported Wasm function itself, with no JS
wrapper on the measured call edge.

These controls retain explicit input bounds checks, signed reader arithmetic,
field-write order and fuel checks. They are **valid-data controls**, not Java
implementations: state is a linear-memory address, widths are packed bytes,
and they omit Java object metadata, class initialization guards, frame spills
and interpreter recovery. They cannot establish Java exception/deoptimization
correctness or runtime parity. This distinction also prevents treating their
absolute difference from TeaVM as a complete cost attribution.

Each worker constructs modules and installs data before its timer, then reads
the stream once. It independently matches checksum `1418269787` and state
`[1,1304428078,87150,87141]` from the original Java oracle. After timing, it
checks negative/end input indices through the selected caller, preserving all
reader fields on failure, and consumes buffered bits with exhausted input.
No measured guest warmup or request wrapping occurs. All three original forms
retain exactly the same generated source and Wasm hashes when the status
variant is added; the common reader source hash is
`159489d1b998dd7383ab16837bcee7ffc903846218b9c8701bd5df6abc9cc911`.

Medians from separate batches, three fresh processes per form, CPU 2, 1-GiB
old-space and eager optimizing Wasm on both controls and TeaVM:

| Batch, ms | Local | Wasm import | Table | Table + status | TeaVM |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Initial | 2.257 | 2.585 | 2.723 | unavailable | 1.759 |
| Repeat | 2.534 | 2.815 | 2.769 | unavailable | 1.752 |
| Status control | 2.256 | 2.888 | 2.741 | 2.743 | 1.743 |
| Status repeat | 2.878 | 2.925 | 2.769 | 2.856 | 1.778 |

The table edge has a modest, variable cost here; it does not reproduce the
actual reader's multi-fold gap. Adding status return/checking does not show a
stable substantial penalty. The last batch's local/table ordering reverses,
so do not infer a precise inlining benefit or a general cross-instance cost
from these short timings. These observations give no reason to rewrite the
runtime return protocol. The remaining object-transfer and entry bookkeeping
need their own controls, matched to emitted code. The excluded code inspection
confirms that the real compact entry consumes an externref metadata global,
checks class readiness, allocates an entry identity, polls fuel and uses a
status/value return; none of those costs is assumed equal to the table edge.

The first original-stream check rejects the control because it omitted the
fixture's final-state checksum fold; the reader state itself already matches.
The fold now runs after timing, as in Java. The status extension's focused test
also catches the missing Binaryen multivalue feature switch before timing.
Neither failure contributes accepted timing evidence. The tests use an
independent bit-string oracle and exercise every call form. Execution tests
require Binaryen `wasm-as` and native JS exception tags; hosts lacking either
report a prerequisite skip. This host passes **10/10 tests with zero skips**.

TeaVM's pinned fixture remains

No fixture, checksum or input is changed to obtain a shorter method.

In this pinned disassembly, TeaVM function `$51` is the helper wrapper: it
loops over widths masked by 31, multiplies the checksum by 33 and directly
calls `$30`. The main dispatcher uses `$51` for the original helper and the
ready-owner version. `$30` is the matching reader, with the same refill loop,
255 mask, field updates and final buffered-bit extraction. It is **not** the
initialization-checking original Bzip reader `$7`, nor the manually inlined
and local source controls `$170`/`$171`.

Our matching exported entry is `canonicalCompactStorageRun`, function `$4`.
Its body spans lines 1052-1971; TeaVM `$30` spans lines 11721-11840. Counts below
are static sites across hot and cold paths, not execution counts or latency:

| Emitted work in matching reader | JVM | TeaVM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Explicit native-base tests for primitive field accesses | 15 | 0 |
| `bufferedBitCount` raw load sites | 4 | 1 |
| Explicit `ref.is_null` sites | 14 | 0 |
| Explicit `if` sites, including fallback/spill/error paths | 47 | 1 |
| Wasm `global.get` / `global.set` sites | 7 / 3 | 0 / 0 |

The meaningful distinction is the proof represented by the instructions:

| Check or operation | TeaVM output | Our output | What may be removed safely |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Object layout / representation | Parameter is `(ref null $19)`; fixed `struct.get` / `struct.set` | Java receiver is `externref`, private metadata is nullable `(ref null $1)`; each primitive access selects linear memory or a checked field helper | A proved native entry/region can fix representation once and remove repeated selection; genuinely unknown metadata retains fallback |
| Receiver null | `struct.get` implicitly traps on null | Explicit metadata/base selection followed by the Java fallback on unsupported/null receivers | A dominating successful access can prove non-null; nullable inputs cannot simply lose their required fault |
| Byte-array index | `array.get_s $14` implicitly checks bounds | Explicit unsigned index/length comparison before `i32.load8_s`, otherwise checked fallback | A range/dominance proof can remove a redundant Java-array check; linear-memory bounds alone do not prove Java-array bounds |
| Repeated bit-count reads | Header `struct.get $19 15` uses `local.tee`; its value is reused in the final subtraction | Repeated guarded `i32.load offset=24` | SSA memory facts can reuse the value when no intervening write or observable fallback can change it |
| Owner readiness | No class-init guard in this reader | Readiness cell test at native entry | A proof of trivial initialization must cover ancestors/native initialization too |
| Scheduling and resumability | No fuel or canonical-frame bookkeeping in this reader | Fuel poll, invocation identity, spill and exception envelope | A bounded-loop/call proof may reduce polling; the VM still must support suspension and exact continuations |

For example, the essential TeaVM field read is:

```wat
(struct.get $19 15 (local.get $1))
```

Our corresponding native/checked selection is:

```wat
(if (result i32)
 (i32.ge_s (local.get $14) (i32.const 0))
 (then (i32.load offset=24 (local.get $14)))
 (else (call $fimport$27 (local.get $1))))
```

The field offset is already known in both compilers. Our missing proof is that
this continuing region can keep using the native representation, plus the
availability of earlier primitive field values. TeaVM's lack of explicit null
or bounds branches must not be mislabeled as a compile-time bounds proof:
those checks are built into its typed GC instructions. WAT size and static
branch counts expose generated work but do not attribute the full loading
ratio to a single category.

The next compiler work should target these specific native-region and
primitive-field SSA proofs. Avoid another broad tuning campaign before showing
that the matched emitted hot path actually loses the identified redundant
work. This comparison and preview provenance are diagnostic only.

### Native primitive-field value proofs: correct code, mixed performance

Starting from retained `8789ccca`, prototype
`4e69af7965ac62c264d48428845248d65940c6aa` implements bounded, normal-flow
must-available definitions for primitive instance fields. It forwards only the
same receiver/physical field definition present on every incoming edge.
Another receiver, arrays, reference fields, calls, volatile accesses and
unknown operations invalidate facts. Loop headers are fresh roots, so
interpreter/fuel re-entry cannot reuse a private snapshot from an earlier run.
Methods with live exception regions keep block-local proofs. Original checked
field accesses still run on every fallback path; no new runtime validity flag
or application-specific opt-in is added.

The analysis is bounded at 32,768 IR nodes, 100,000 transfer visits and 64
captured definitions. It runs after demotion discovery and discards incomplete
proofs. The first version uses independent locals for native snapshots. The
refinement, `a00e61e0d56ef1f1724e74eaf2c72a788e4472a8`, reuses the producer's SSA
local. If the allocator had shared its physical slot, that value is pinned to
a unique slot before final emission and before constructing resume bindings.
Stackified store operands retain a capture at their original native store.

The initial focused suite passes **1075/1075 assertions**, and the refined
suite **1076/1076**. Coverage includes native/fallback getter order and thrown
identity, setters that mutate another field, aliasing receivers, observable
array callbacks, volatile barriers, inherited shadowed fields, joins with
matching and differing definitions, wide integers, floating values, partial
effects before failure, handler snapshots, capture budgets and graph cleanup.
A real loop-resume test mutates the field between several native runs and
compares exact final state with the unoptimized control. An initial test
incorrectly compared two different receiver identities in an exception
snapshot; it is corrected to use the same receiver.

### Private typed-entry representation proof

Prototype `bd1eccd7a0f2b7f05562854f9288495774f42d16`, on
`java-tools` branch `experiment/teavm-native-parity`, adapts the earlier entry
specialization to the retained typed-storage ABI. The rolling control remains
`8789cccad5c3b6bc22d585f0a58082de5d44ea08`. This is an experimental source
snapshot, not the selected bundle, deployed runtime or a parity claim.

The private storage parameter already has GC type `(ref null $1)`, proving its
structural layout at compilation/validation. The internal caller validates heap
ownership when producing this hidden argument; the GC type alone does not prove
ownership of an arbitrary payload supplied by a host. At entry, one guard checks that
metadata exists and its immutable base denotes native object storage. The
selected body can use that base and GC reference storage directly. It does
not repeat object metadata fills or native-versus-checked field selection.
It does not hoist Java field values or a host metadata lookup. Unknown, null,
foreign and reference-array metadata take the original checked body. Ordinary,
legacy compact and resume entries keep the original lowering.

The extra native body is capped at 4 KiB and still shares the existing 16 KiB
compact-entry duplication limit. Unsupported exception/deoptimization/resume
shapes retain their existing compilation path. No application names or new
runtime opt-in flag are introduced. The clone may allocate extra scratch
locals, so its private export receives its own declaration list; ordinary
functions retain their original declarations and indices.

The focused suite passes **1401/1401 assertions**. The dedicated new file passes
**154/154**. Coverage includes native/plain/mixed/foreign receivers, null and
bounds exceptions, partial writes, getter ordering, reference replacement,
wide values, exact fuel spill state, resume after replacing a field container,
active-body replacement, budget exhaustion, ordinary-body byte equality and
collection of the proof/SSA graph. A reference-array field loop explicitly
exercises scratch locals allocated only while cloning.

The matching original-reader WAT has JVM module SHA-256
`61c93e2b24eaf14d1600c7aa65a4ac0971d7ee4c8897ab789a77969cdae5eb8d`.
The unchanged TeaVM artifact is
`5beb55421087681123409c3cfe790fc0e3f13fc885f9718d48197d5766cffc81`.
In JVM private export `$4`, the selected native body has **zero** per-field
receiver-storage tests, versus **15** in its checked body and in the old body;
one receiver selection remains before the selected body. Its byte-array
storage selection is separate and still remains. The native body has eight
`if` sites versus TeaVM reader `$30`'s one; these counts include cold paths,
not dynamic CPU attribution.

TeaVM's absence of explicit null/bounds branches is not a compile-time proof
that every input is non-null and in range: `struct.get` and `array.get_s`
include runtime checks. Typed storage proves layout; moving representation
selection to entry needs an invariant; eliminating array bounds checks needs
a separate range/dominance proof. The prototype preserves array bounds,
readiness, scheduling/fuel and exception behavior.

### GC scalar-state control and TeaVM exception policy

A smaller control, `buffered-call-gc-parameter`, moves the six scalar state
slots to a mutable GC struct, behind one extra immutable metadata pointer.
It retains the original request sequence, linear-memory byte input, explicit
unsigned Java-index check, fuel accounting and native table/status returns.
This tests field representation rather than quietly removing checks. Like
the existing controls it models valid data, not every JVM fallback. The
independent bit-string oracle, negative/end bounds exceptions, unchanged
state before failed writes, zero-refill case and invalid metadata tests pass.
The focused fixture/statistics command passes **10/10**, zero skips. An initial
WAT forward-type declaration failure is fixed by declaring the field payload
before the metadata type. All seven previous controls retain their original
generated sources; that one-time compatibility check happened before the
user requested no more unchanged-baseline rechecks.

The first GC-state median is **2.842 ms**, versus previously recorded typed
linear-state control 2.973 ms and TeaVM 2.084 ms in that set. A subsequent
candidate-only set is **6.687 ms** (6.687, 6.594, 6.863), despite identical
caller/provider Wasm hashes. Preserve both sets: this is not evidence of a
stable GC-field gain and does not justify a whole-runtime representation
rewrite. The new caller/provider hashes are respectively
`3c3ace09cc170a5924d7da51f3e1a89d9f44e907fed527d1265806821ac955a9` and
`2e422a415e6fe2258eba6849e7ad19fcb127de8c5ca11bcb1d486974a64e1c32`.
The observations are nested under `typedNativeEntryProof.gcScalarStateControl`.

**Correction to the check comparison above:** GC instructions check for null
and out-of-range access by trapping, but that is not the same as delivering
catchable Java `NullPointerException` / `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
TeaVM 0.16.0's [WasmGCTarget insertion passes](https://github.com/konsoletyper/teavm/blob/0.16.0/core/src/main/java/org/teavm/backend/wasm/WasmGCTarget.java#L225-L234)
run null/bounds insertion only with `strict` enabled. The
[Maven default](https://github.com/konsoletyper/teavm/blob/0.16.0/tools/maven/plugin/src/main/java/org/teavm/maven/TeaVMCompileMojo.java#L98-L99)
is `false`; the loading, microbench and Vorbis fixture POM generators do not
enable it. Installed 0.16.0 core/plugin bytecode confirms both the conditional
passes and default. Thus missing explicit checks cannot all be attributed to
compile-time proofs. The previous artifacts, timings and 1.10x target remain
unchanged; do not disable JVM Java exceptions to imitate this policy.
This finding comes from source/configuration inspection, not a baseline rerun.

### Bounds facts from an earlier native array access

Experimental source `01019d2630c9735645e45f064066b23a22bbc8d5` adds a
block-local bounds proof. Refinement
`3be507be60a8f60db146e6d21fdcc2d562b3c10a` also recognizes equal total i32
subscript expressions rather than requiring the exact same SSA node.
Both are saved on `java-tools` branch `experiment/teavm-native-parity`.
The retained baseline remains `8789ccca`.

A normally completed primitive access establishes: either this captured
array base is negative (the checked fallback ran), or its index is within
its captured length. A later access to the same array/index/element width
in the same basic block keeps the native-versus-checked selection. In its
native arm the earlier fact proves the bounds check redundant; in its
checked arm the original import still checks each access. This specifically
preserves host getters that shrink an ordinary array between operations.
A store can change an element without changing that bounds fact, so this
proof does not forward the earlier element value.

Facts do not cross block boundaries, calls, field operations, other unknown
effects or generation-checked field-array metadata. Equal expression keys
include only total integer operations, numeric constants and opaque SSA
leaves. Java i32 wrapping is preserved; differently computed/updated indices
retain their checks. Discovery is capped at 50,000 work units, 128 available
facts per block, expression depth six, 1,024 memo entries per block and 256
characters per expression key. Exceeding the work budget discards the entire
proof. No execution flag, new runtime local, validity test, cloned method body
or application-specific rule is introduced.

The initial focused suite passes **626/626 assertions**; the refined suite
**639/639**. The new test file contributes **86**, covering all primitive widths,
wide precision, signed overflow, distinct expressions, changed indices, nulls,
negative/large bounds, checked getter order and dynamic lengths, foreign heaps,
partial writes before failure, floating NaN/infinity/negative zero, loop
behavior and collection of the proof/SSA graph. Numeric `ldc` constants initially
cleared the proof between a read and float/long store; the analysis now treats
those primitive constants as total. String/class constants keep the barrier.
Existing array-ABI, copying and loop-resume suites validate the changed compiler.

### Native array invariants and entry range proofs (2026-10-22)

The unchanged runtime and TeaVM baselines are reused. No baseline correctness,
identity or timing run is needed merely to establish that the baseline is still
itself. `run-jvm` measures changed candidates in fresh processes against the
existing immutable HotSpot/PCM oracles. Generated artifacts remain outside Git.

A controlled native-Wasm model compares linear float storage and GC float-array
storage using the same metadata shape, arithmetic, explicit bounds errors, fuel
polling, initialization and one-pass workload. These models deliberately omit
VM representation selection and frame transport; they are not JVM performance
or parity results. The generator is `apps/loading/float-array-controls.mjs`.
At eight million butterflies, readback medians are 24.193 ms for linear storage
and 27.606 ms for GC storage with an independent stored length. Encoding the
bounds-error import as non-returning gives 21.749 ms for linear storage; GC with
physical `array.len` gives 25.720 ms, or 20.994 ms when the error is also
non-returning. No-readback medians respectively are 27.361, 26.477, 24.186,
28.003 and 23.584 ms. Samples and outliers remain in the existing report. This
does not justify a GC-array backend rewrite. It supports giving the native
compiler accurate representation, length and error-flow information instead.

Stage C, `19243e3a6da8700bbcdd4fd750fd03ad4453be98`, adds a bounded, generic

indices use the same proof. Unknown or negative indices retain their checked
operations; a short array selects the untouched original body. Boolean arrays
keep their checked storage and cannot prevent independently proved float arrays
from using the native version. Merely forwarding an array header does not
request an unnecessary version. The source analysis stops after 50,000 nodes.

#### Total numeric loop invariants: rejected component experiment

The first proof (`1128de04c80196cf851acba34bdfb4a07fa993bd`) passed its focused
correctness checks but refused expanded bytecode. Its separate code diagnostic
found zero moved transform values and unchanged transform WAT. It was **not
timed**. The expanded-SSA proof (`d4881f19f2299830a45781e044d7ae90caff67ab`)
proved the invariant slice using SSA dependencies and dominance and moved **66
values, including constants**, into loop preheaders. It uses dedicated locals
because the original block-local allocator did not account for longer lifetimes.
The diagnostic output is exact; its module SHA-256 is
`1e1cc46d3dc8a757b1e53bd6c4ce86583243f72e5f69f8c49a99f47f8338d9a7`.

This proof moves only total numeric operations, retaining their original
arithmetic tree. It never hoists loads, calls or integer division; it neither
reassociates floats nor removes bounds/representation checks. Limits are 256
blocks, 32 loops, 256 moved values, 50,000 analysis work and depth 64. Split
irreducible regions, demotions and inline deopt stubs retain their existing code.
Tests cover nested/branch-local availability, wide arithmetic, NaN/signed zero,
zero trips, integer faults, partial array effects, handler/fuel snapshots,
expanded SSA, external native resumption, cleanup and excessive/cyclic proofs.

### Guard one native static-array body: positive component result, not promoted

`3829e0f688dcd3733b5409df5bb45ed6734b221c` tests a different representation
strategy from the rejected cloned leaf/loop versions. An eligible substantial,
callback-free static numeric kernel gets **one native body**, rather than a
native clone beside a generic body. Entry guards check ordinary field-cell
capabilities, genuine owned array headers in this memory and class readiness.
A failed guard spills the original entry and uses the existing interpreter/OSR
handoff before any Java effects. It never calls customized getters early.
Every native bounds check and original numeric operation remains. Source and
return references, field writes, allocations, untrusted calls and live exception
regions refuse this first proof. Math intrinsics use the compiler's existing
pure-intrinsic classification, not a new general host-callback assumption.

Captured base/length metadata follows native reference phis with simultaneous
copies, including swaps and cycles. Compiled callers are explicitly told that
entry can refuse, so a caller cannot pin an unconditional non-exiting call.
External native resumption is disabled for this specialized body: fuel/guard
handoffs retain the existing saved Java frame and finish through the supported
fallback. Replacing a field during suspension must not replace its captured old
array. This sacrifices a resume opportunity in exchange for a bounded, auditable
first experiment; fallback performance is not automatically accepted.

Discovery is bounded to 4,096 nodes, 16 static array cells, 128 reference values
and 50,000 reference-analysis work. The substantial-kernel threshold is 128
nodes/16 array sites. Metadata graphs release after translation; replacing an
array permits collection while compiled modules remain live. No application
identifier, public flag or generated artifact is added to java-tools.

### Native array regions and readiness reuse: implemented, not promoted

`9aa5104d16c7250a2f127a203bff7e6fae9d55b8` extends the single-body proof to
closed CFG regions. Candidate discovery is generic: good blocks contain numeric
operations, primitive array operations, authenticated static array reads or the
existing pure Math intrinsics. A region has one entry block, no outside edges
into its other blocks and no successful callback/initializer/allocation/field
write inside. Live exception regions, inlining, irreducible splits, demotions
and existing guarded-loop plans are conservatively excluded in this first pass.
Discovery is bounded to 256 method blocks, 128 blocks per region, 16 candidates,
four disjoint selected regions and 50,000 analysis work. Known null/boolean
storage is refused. Existing generic code remains outside selected regions.

Guards execute on **outside edges after simultaneous reference phi copies**,
not on internal backedges. They validate static-cell readiness/capabilities and
owned array headers, then authenticate already-captured incoming references
through allocator metadata without invoking host getters. Captured references
are not silently replaced with their current field values. Private base/length
locals prevent introducing early parameter length queries or lending a proof
to generic accesses after callbacks. Internal phi metadata copies are parallel,
including cycles and entry-header backedges. Refusal spills at that region's
entry, without replaying earlier effects or prefix allocations. External native
resumption is disabled so that it cannot bypass a guard. Bounds checks remain.

The original packet decoder selects the previously identified two regions:
43 blocks/69 array sites and 28 blocks/23 sites, **92 sites total**. The first
needs five captured incoming array references and one static cell; the second
uses nine static cells. A separate original-sample inspection records 682

object/array ownership hands off before any Java effect. The proof accepts only
native primitive fields and directly read primitive-array fields, refuses
volatile fields, reference writes, calls, allocation and exception regions, and
keeps bounds checks and fuel suspension. External native resume is disabled so
continuations cannot bypass the entry proof. Primitive stores retain their
original order; no primitive field-value forwarding is added.

### Expose known memory limits: compile-only evidence

WasmHeap creates memories with a known physical maximum and normally reserves
that maximum initially. Generated structured modules nevertheless import
`(memory 1)`, withholding that fact from the native compiler. This is separate
from the withdrawn capture pass. Before changing the runtime, reassemble its
saved matched WAT twice, with the existing declaration and with
`(memory 4096 4096)`. Compile both using Node 22.23.2, eager TurboFan and native
code printing; instantiate neither and execute **no guest code**. Only the
memory declaration differs. This is new compiler-output evidence, not another
baseline correctness or timing run.

The same function (index 73) has **20,300** native instruction bytes with the
existing declaration and **19,752** with fixed limits. The inline canonical
companion is 20,572 versus 20,484 bytes. The main native stack reservation grows
from 0x178 to 0x180 bytes, so smaller code is not a claim of less spilling or a
speed result. These observations justify testing the missing type information,
not attributing the full loading gap to it.

The successful compile-only command pipes WAT through
`wasm-as - --all-features --disable-compact-imports -o -`, then constructs a
`WebAssembly.Module` under
`node --no-liftoff --no-wasm-lazy-compilation --print-wasm-code --print-wasm-code-function-index=73`.
Native output occupies the existing scratch log only. An initial missing stdin
argument and then Binaryen's newer compact-import encoding prevented compilation;
using `-` and disabling that encoding fixes this diagnostic. Neither failed
attempt executes a workload. No generated binaries or assembly enter Git.

### Transitive field-write proof through fixed instance calls

summary returns unknown for every nested instance call. `VorbisCodebook.readVector`
calls final `readScalar`, which in turn updates only two static bit-reader
cursors. Unknown effects unnecessarily invalidate the residue caller's field
caches. This follows the existing code/import evidence; no new CPU profile or
unchanged-baseline execution is used.

fallback when the previous instance summary is unknown. It follows static calls
and instance targets fixed by final/private methods or a final symbolic owner.
It resolves loaded inheritance without speculative CHA, executes nothing, and
rejects unknown, overridable, native, synchronized, special/interface/dynamic

publish incomplete per-callee summaries. At most 64 methods and 50,000 units of
analysis are examined; exhaustion returns unknown. Only field names/descriptors
are retained, matching the existing conservative cache invalidation keys. Array
element cache invalidation, class-init guards, exceptions, fuel and fallback
protocols remain in place. There is no application identifier or opt-in flag.

### Resumable inline loop activations

The preceding feasibility finding is implemented in isolated runtime candidate
`2f27b82ed207f54c788c6e8a80422e8df02d9850`. Refined child
`df1fb75a7762bb70e33300f47e4a8606085e2fff` restricts the new admission path to
bodies containing an actual backward edge. It does not enable deep inlining or
raise the existing per-callee/caller code budgets. This is generic JVM code with
no application identities or new user options. The backend supplies the internal
capability only when existing canonical frame handoffs and native JS exception
tags are available; unsupported configurations keep their established path.

A root instance-loop body may now retain its nested calls and carry the original
callee PC, relocated local-slot range and caller operand-prefix length. Fuel
polling remains active for these loops. On fuel exhaustion, a demoted instruction
or a nested-call handoff, the compiler materializes a real callee frame at its
precise bytecode PC and restores the outer frame at the instruction AFTER the
invoke. The operand prefix stays with its original caller, including references
and category-2 values; the remaining stack belongs to the child. Deeper pending
canonical children precede this new frame in the existing handoff chain. Normal
execution allocates no new JavaScript activation. Closures retain scalar spill
plans and original method metadata, not compiler/SSA graphs or donated frames.

Meaningful callee exception handlers and synchronized methods remain excluded
from splicing. Exceptions from the inlined body use the existing outer-call PC
mapping; after a yield, the real interpreted child unwinds through the normal
Java handler path. New loop sites in live OUTER handler ranges can use that
mapping without broadening admission of the older loop-free shapes. Fixed final
methods/final symbolic owners no longer carry a class-epoch speculation record:
later valid Java subclasses cannot change those implementations. This is needed
for the recovered normal-flow body to remain eligible for canonical native calls;
open dispatch retains its checks and speculation metadata.

yield, and collection of donated child frames while compiled modules stay live.
Existing canonical-frame, receiver-ranking, compiler-retention, structured-resume,
deep/instance inlining and handler suites also pass.

### Flattening the short static helper inside a recovered loop

Candidate `f2c8ad04a4b035ee863cd3abc29ae44c5b88f083` builds on the tested recovery
framework `b8fc713`. A recoverable root instance loop can now splice an acyclic,
bytecode-backed static leaf without requiring deep inlining. It reuses the
existing per-callee and total expansion budgets. Calls with native/synchronized
implementations, meaningful handlers, casts, unsupported operations or backward
edges retain their ordinary call path. Non-intrinsic nested guest calls also
prevent leaf admission. There are no application identities or new user flags.

Here "atomic" means the leaf has no internal fuel/guest-call handoff; Java
exceptions still occur after any preceding stores. A loop-header entry marker
retains the enclosing original activation and call PC, so a zero-argument helper
at the first instruction of a loop cannot accidentally suppress its fuel poll.
Leaf scratch slots sit outside that activation's original local range and need
not be donated when execution yields later at the enclosing loop header.

The helper's owner is an explicit readiness dependency, even when its body
reads no static fields or the owner has no explicit initializer. Existing entry
readiness guards only test the token: a cold owner returns to the original
outer entry without executing guest effects or initializing it early. Original
bytecode then performs first-use initialization at the helper invocation after
any prefixes. Untaken/zero-trip dependencies remain uninitialized. Warm bodies
retain the dependency so an initialization reset cannot bypass the guard.
This is conservative cold fallback, not early class initialization.

The focused 13-file suite passes **1,117/1,117 assertions**, no skips. New tests
exercise cold and warm composition, an untaken helper, initializer observation
of a prior prefix, no-static-field dependencies after readiness reset, partial
array stores before bounds/null faults, a fuel yield at a helper call in the
loop header, a later fault after suspension, and real handler-bearing helper
continuations. Existing recovery, canonical ownership, cold inlining, expansion
budget, receiver, exception and retention tests also pass.

Two fixture assumptions were corrected before that pass: class initialization
correctly resets the leaf's static fields, so input is supplied through the
already initialized probe class and read by the real initializer; and a caught
fault in a non-inlined helper correctly donates its handler continuation instead
of returning synchronously. Early failures are not counted as passes.

## Local callback-effect proofs and terminal cast selection (2026-10-23)

The prior process-wide callback protocol regressed loading. The next prototype,

version conditions, without retaining callee metadata, old exports or SSA graphs.
Unknown calls fence before invocation. A canonical binding's version changes
on target replacement, withdrawal or release; saturation declines new proofs
and physical slot reuse creates an independent condition. Do not weaken this
rule merely because two bodies appear equivalent.

JavaScript replacements, bound functions and proxies do not receive it. Whole
normal-return proofs reject volatile fields, handlers, reference writes and

### Loop-entry array type proof (2026-10-23)

This experiment addresses the measured cost of local per-cast proof state. It
uses one integer validity local for a bounded, callback-free natural loop.
The compiler proves the absence of reference writes, allocations and unknown
callbacks; the entry checks private array/object ownership, current and saved
references, static capabilities and captured native callee versions. Positive
casts return the original reference. Negative entry checks execute the original
checked cast imports in the same Wasm body, preserving host getter/throwable
behavior. There is still one branch per selected cast; this is not a claim that
all checks were removed. Array bounds, original fuel checks and resume points
remain. Resume entry validates the saved references again, without replaying
prefix effects. No game information, runtime opt-in flag, loop clone or per-call
cast epoch is added to java-tools.

Initial source `b4576a25d4ff8fd472b9293092aa4376c5989374` selected an 11-block
inner loop: 35,280 entry queries and 578,537 remaining checked integer casts in
the original ready-owner archive diagnostic. It was not timed. A separate shape
trace showed duplicate field and incoming-phi dependencies exhausting the
16-source budget for the enclosing loop. Source
`6a898dac4f691840604a09d1dff4df2b9f78af8e` deduplicates equivalent private-storage
recipes and validates current header-phi references instead of redundant outside
incoming values. It preserves the budget. The original decoder now selects a

entry queries, three successful guards and 30 checked integer casts**, with
checksum `-1415522687`, zero exits/throws and zero late compilation. Instrumented
elapsed times are excluded from performance comparisons.

storage obtained by the array's own read with null while retaining its valid
base. Copy captured field storage only when available. The separate reference
array test covers repeated native array reads through a plain receiver's getter;
the new region tests cover checked getter ordering, exact host throwable identity,
wrong/foreign arrays, row budget, reference phi swaps, native callee replacement,
resumed saved matrices and collection of compiler graphs and completed Java
arrays. The focused 11-file set passes **1203/1203** assertions; after dependency

### Revocable boolean storage without per-call validation (2026-10-23)

The previous loop-entry cast turn made progress by finding a real cache bug and
rejecting a component-only speedup. The next experiment uses existing reader and
boolean evidence, not new CPU attribution or unchanged baseline/oracle runs.
The rejected boolean implementation repeatedly validated ordinary TypedArray
metadata at short method boundaries (saved native-path control median 78.997 ms,
saved checked-path control 109.771 ms). That cost is distinct from its efficient
large parameter loop. TeaVM's typed boolean arrays need neither this JS metadata
boundary nor repeated descriptor checks.

Source `e3bc5a10260e49a4b126b0c3172b649816f4f0a7` gives allocator-created boolean
arrays a revocable capability. The existing two-word array header carries a
negative encoded pointer to **eight native bytes per array**: validity and data
base. Boolean Wasm accesses check validity, retain Java bounds/fuel behavior,
normalize nonzero loads and mask stores. Metadata edits revoke validity before
any host callback; a cached pointer can therefore fall back at the original
access even when other caches survive the callback. Future metadata queries
refuse the revoked pointer. Signed bytes and booleans keep distinct semantics;
known nonboolean byte sources do not get the additional boolean arm. Static
and instance headers are reused; there is no per-call scratch publication,
descriptor query, epoch or new user option. Missing ownership, spent heaps or
unavailable reclamation retain checked storage.

A draft that revoked only published headers was replaced before timing: local
copies can outlive a host callback. The final capability word covers those
copies directly and eliminates subscriber lists. Its wrapper is weakly indexed,
uses ordinary heap finalization, and never exposes raw backing storage through
callback array arguments or self-returning TypedArray methods. Species/custom
join methods revoke before their receiver could escape. The supported array
recognizer, generated JS lookup, Java clone, class transport and portable state
codec recognize the wrapper. Portable state preserves backing bytes and sharing;
workers transport a view rather than attempting to clone a Proxy. This is a
representation experiment, not proof of all browser/native integration surfaces.
It does not remove every runtime check or claim that public host metadata is a
compile-time constant.

file passes **90/90**, including additional interop and real fuel-slice tests.
Tests cover noncanonical backing bytes, masked stores, zero import/query counts
across 1,000 actual native helper entries, instance fields, a host callback
revoking an already-cached pointer, exact throwable identity/getter ordering,
reference sharing, Java clone, worker packets, snapshots, weak ownership and
collection. Forced three-unit slices revoke metadata between native entries,
preserve all 64 preceding effects exactly once, return the correct result,
release the frame and compile no Java during execution. Test-only child
`01b3827ac5a230145c55eff800b065b45e9b71b4` preserves that extra fuel coverage;
performance observations retain the runtime revision actually executed.

A final **read-only inspection of the saved TeaVM WAT** resolves that hypothesis
without executing either backend. Its field-call loop is function `$162`: it
updates the `sum*33` checksum and calls `$55(i&1023, 1)`. Helper `$55` branches on

calls `$55(i, depth-1)`. Both call boundaries remain in the saved WAT. Thus
literal-depth recursion elimination by TeaVM's Java-to-Wasm compiler is **not**
the explanation for this control. No baseline hash, rebuild or execution runs.

shapes, using compile-only inspection or a new tiny linked-call model. Do not
repeat the failed boolean implementation or assume a whole-module linker will
help before that comparison demonstrates a relevant difference.

### Deferred native-object identities: original-workload screen (2026-10-23)

Native inspection of the captured reader identifies unconditional per-call
invocation-ID allocation before guest work. A normal direct return creates no
JavaScript frame, yet updates the counter, checks wrap and carries the ID for
possible spills. TeaVM's reader has no corresponding VM protocol. Test whether
moving this work to its actual use matters, rather than inferring cost from the
static instruction-byte difference.

compiler-proven callback-free native-object body. Its compact native export

before writing frame locals or operand stacks. Such a body cannot reenter guest
code or resume internally after a spill. Ordinary JS entry still uses identity
zero; legacy canonical wrappers and all other bodies retain eager IDs. Throw-only
exits keep their existing exact throwable/owner protocol without inventing a
frame. No new option, guard, epoch or game-specific name is introduced.

suspended frames with independent IDs, receivers, arguments and exact PCs;

callee refusals; merely tagging a callee pure or preserving an old cached base
is insufficient. Read the saved local-callback and whole-Wasm failures before

needed to start this proof audit.

### Precise instruction refusal for native object loops

Candidate `9b2be24d3aa697b5dd3fcd8b7ebadb64b13f42e3` implements the operand-prefix
prerequisite identified above. Shared SSA accepts an internal predicate selecting
additional throwing instructions whose operand prefix must survive a retry.
Existing calls and monitors retain their snapshots automatically. Ordinary SSA
consumers do not acquire extra snapshots. Trivial-phi pruning rewrites the new
snapshots, and existing local allocation/stackification protects their values.
This is an internal analysis interface, not an environment or user flag.

The structured compiler's new `emitInstructionExit` uses the existing exact
retry/frame-ownership protocol: spill locals reaching this instruction, restore
its operand prefix and operands, and return its original item index. It marks
the operation deoptable so callers cannot assume a never-exiting raw link.
Missing/unkinded snapshots and unrecoverable inline positions refuse compilation.
The established inline-activation machinery is reused by the emitter, but the
native-body admission in this pass still excludes inlined bodies; it does not
claim new inline selection or callback-safe metadata lifetimes.

### First-use receiver proofs and native loop reconstruction

Experimental source `49edf676d05df77a444e835d1d17223c3d18b187` expands the
callback-free native object-loop body to multiple receivers and receiver phis.
The certified-helper refinement is `b02295818157295821c029130e22a84ef906627a`;
final test-only child is `d7158fbd78cc32c46c449635c0f0d58bb58d1f9f`.
The established single-parameter form keeps its existing entry policy. Newly
admitted shapes authenticate receivers at the actual field read/write, using
the exact instruction continuation from the preceding pass. Zero-trip loops
and untaken null receivers need no lookup or dereference. There is one native
body, no user flag, and no application-specific core identity.

The proof remains bounded to 256 body nodes, 32 field sites, four distinct
receiver/array-field pairs, eight receiver SSA values and 64 nodes in receiver
provenance. Receiver sources must resolve to parameters, nulls or reference
phis; unsupported sources, volatile fields, reference writes, meaningful
handlers and calls still refuse admission. Existing SSA cache kills invalidate
receiver ownership when a phi is redefined. Array headers are captured per
loaded array SSA value, rather than per current receiver/field. Re-reading a
source resets its captured/ownership flags.

New first-use guards **do not trust private transport metadata** from a general
caller: it may have run a callback since capturing that metadata. They query
the current wrapper and require a canonical field container. A red semantic
test demonstrates why identity alone is insufficient: adding an own field
getter preserves container identity but changes Java field access. The new
`validatedNativeObjectStorageOf` rejects changed prototypes, extra own entries,
shadowing accessors and inconsistent primitive/native bases, without invoking
getters. A frozen layout token is shared by the class; each field-storage
record adds one token pointer. Malformed stores return no certificate.

A non-null validated result explicitly guarantees the canonical GC store and
its nonnegative base, matching named field access. Final lowering uses that
contract instead of emitting a second negative-base branch and duplicate cold
spill at each new field guard. This new certificate is stronger than the old
private metadata transport. Future callee proofs must not infer it merely from
an older native-body site count or an incoming store argument.

The new lazy receiver form can share its native loop body with a proved resume
entry. Fresh Wasm locals force ownership reconstruction after suspension.
Source audit identified another required case: a field read before the loop
can be skipped on resume, and that field may subsequently refer to a different
array. The first resumed array access therefore queries owned metadata for the
**restored original array value**, using the existing allocation registry with
no length getter. It never substitutes the receiver's current field header.
The test changes that field from `[3]` to `[100]` after yielding; the resumed
four-iteration calculation correctly retains its captured array and returns
40. Receiver-container replacement after a yield refuses at the exact field
and continues through Java without replaying earlier writes.

### Closed native calls with publication-bound ownership contracts

The next compiler change is archived at `592d30caac97d1a1594d6b938c2b0034f5354320`
on the experimental JVM ref. It does not replace the measured comparator or a
production artifact. There is no new runtime option or application-specific
rule. Ordinary canonical eligibility is deliberately insufficient for this
new calling convention.

A dedicated `canonicalClosedStorageRun` export accepts private stores whose
ownership the caller has validated. Its certificate is bound to the method
identity, object-parameter positions, and **that exact instantiated export**.
Restricted canonical table slots publish only matching certificates. Withdrawal
or an incompatible replacement installs a pure Wasm refusal (`-7`), with no
JavaScript bridge or guest effects. The caller then reconstructs the original
invoke, including pending operands and preceding field writes. Publication
updates the table; this does not introduce a generation comparison at every
call.

The native proof now composes eligible static calls, including acyclic
forwarders. It still rejects arbitrary callbacks, reference writes, volatile
fields and unsupported exception regions. A mixed caller validates object
ownership once at first use, then its compatible callees reuse the private
store. A forwarding body's **ordinary** entry keeps its existing path: merely
adding a certificate must not add a shape lookup to every old reader call.
The closed entry uses a reserved internal fresh-entry mode, sharing the existing
16 KiB aggregate body-duplication budget. Larger entries use the existing wrapper
mechanism. No additional user flag is required.

The first integration run exposed an initialization bug in the proposed
composition: the old block-level cold-call guard ran before completed prefix
writes. Restricted calls now rely on the callee wrapper's own readiness check
and refuse at the actual invoke. Another fixture showed that a dependency can
become eligible during discovery, after speculative field snapshots were
pruned. A bounded one-time fresh translation restores the required snapshots,
releasing the discarded graph and table slots first. Neither failed run is
counted as successful validation.

### Closed regions in mixed decoders and SSA certificate transport

The previous closed-call capability had no ordinary-entry root in the loading
graph. This pass implements a bounded region proof in generic JVM code; no game
identity, priority map or runtime opt-in is added. Mixed methods can enter and
leave a union of eligible basic blocks. Private receiver, array and cast facts
start untrusted, are invalidated on outside-to-inside edges, and are killed or
transported when SSA values change. Partial methods never publish a whole-body
closed certificate or trusted export.

The first version, `6e29fe2fc0e3406026b523e44325f8d0a707c3d9`, reaches the actual
archive decoder: the full preparation census has 708 entry/callee rows and
admits 26 closed calls across 104 blocks of `Bzip2Decoder.decodeBlocks`. This
census executes no Java ticks or asset requests. A changed execution diagnostic
matches checksum `-1415522687`, compiles no guest code, and actually enters the
closed reader 490948 times (plus 320218 closed `readBit` entries and 40 closed
`readByte` entries).

That first placement is a **performance failure**. Three candidate-only fresh
archive processes take 267.053, 237.653 and 261.492 ms; median **261.492 ms**,
versus saved current-comparator samples 40.807995, 41.699230 and 40.140670 ms
(median **40.807995 ms**). The excluded diagnostic records **634811 strict
object validations**: conservative boundaries fragmented the hot loop. None of
these measurements reruns the baseline or TeaVM, and this source is not selected
as the measured baseline or published.

At `111b80058414dce19e18f238643d2ee67da1aec1`, primitive array accesses may acquire
an owned header from their **actual SSA value**, including outside captures and
loop-carried arrays. A side-effect-free allocation-registry query refuses
foreign/plain arrays at their exact access, preserving completed child calls
and operand prefixes. The changed diagnostic admits 108 blocks and adds only
three owned-header queries, but leaves object validations at 634811. That
observation rejects array provenance alone as the explanation; no timing cohort
is spent on that insufficient refinement.

Source inspection identifies repeated array casts and native static array
reads inside the decode loop. At `1e0e703c61c8e0810f10a0b4c737c1ce2805d34d`, a
primitive-array cast earns a combined class/header certificate from owned
metadata and a plain own type descriptor, without invoking a getter. Null
casts succeed; a later null array access still fails at its original instruction.
A failed cast proof exits at the cast and uses the existing Java check. Boolean
arrays remain excluded from this raw-array proof. Canonical static reference
cells use their existing native value/header and a readiness/cell-validity
guard at the actual `getstatic`. Cold initialization and customized getters
retain exact preceding effects. Their block-level guard must not initialize a
dependency before a completed prefix.

The proof also admits these casts under default compiler policy. Discovery can
emit the existing checked cast for a proved candidate. If its callee becomes
ready only during discovery, one bounded retry restores the cast snapshots and
reconsiders only the corresponding cast demotion. Snapshot plans are released
with the other compiler analyses. No environment switch is needed.

This version admits 118 blocks, nine casts and six static reads. It reduces
object validations to **8795**, but still executes **512016 cast/header queries**.
That new diagnostic determines the next change: proofs were discarded at SSA
joins even when the reference value was simply being carried onward.

At `b4c540061ed46e302a9b87f97f6fdc593690000c`, a bounded upstream closure (maximum
256 value/type pairs) provides certificate locals for needed SSA joins. Edge
emission snapshots source certificates before any phi target is killed, then
installs them in parallel with the corresponding reference assignments. This
handles swaps without lending one array's proof to another. Unsupported edges
still revoke every certificate. A successful cast also seeds its result's
owned-array header, so its following access needs no second query.

The original archive diagnostic now has **8795 object validations, 10248
cast/header queries, and three separate owned-array-header queries**. It uses
30 cast certificate records for nine cast sites. Checksum and zero guest

### One guarded body for static integer state and owned arrays

The prior region/phi turn made concrete progress: it created a used decoder
root and exposed an unsuccessful full-loading result. The next change follows
its source inspection rather than repeating baseline timing or CPU profiling.
The existing native-array whole-body proof rejected scalar static stores, so
it could not cover the original music reader's byte/bit cursor updates.

Experimental source `53e84b195a40cc45a5cb69d23a6b04c425113546` adds a generic
bounded whole-body proof for static methods with primitive parameters, readonly
native static array references, at least two integer stores and actual array
accesses. It rejects opaque calls, reference writes, volatile cells, meaningful
handlers, unsupported/inlined shapes and exhausted budgets (256 nodes, eight
array fields, eight integer cells and bounded array-reference provenance).
There is no application identity or opt-in flag.

The entry checks owner readiness, each cell's required read/write permissions,
and owned array headers without running a getter. Every integer write updates
canonical memory at its original Java instruction and resets the existing JS
representation tag. A failed guard executes no prefix and uses the supported
Java continuation. Cold dependencies therefore initialize at their original
instruction, after any prefix that Java would have performed.

Stateful bodies retain the existing native loop-resume proof. Resumed guards
refuse at the saved header, never the method prefix. A reference captured before
the loop obtains its owned header from the **restored original array value**;
it does not substitute a subsequently replaced global field. Entry revocation
by a foreign array or customized cell falls back with exact captured state.
The old readonly transform proof and its established resume policy are unchanged.

Inspection of the already-cached TeaVM WAT identifies the original music
readers by their signatures, shared byte/bit/data globals, one/two signed byte
reads and three cursor writes (`$58` and `$29`). TeaVM retains cursor values in
locals between immediate global stores. At
`51e7d3026b8b41c4c0e9ca20b0a0357486f6ccaa`, the new proof uses one invocation-local
integer value per read cell. Every store still writes immediately, while
subsequent native reads use that value until invocation/resume exit. No
untrusted continuing callback or owned-array alias can invalidate it inside
the admitted body. The scalar discovery graph is released with compiler analyses.

### Mixed readonly instance arrays, static state and terminal reference loads

The next proof is generic rather than a game-identity rule. Runtime source
`1ce255a534a5a7aca36bca282ed2305f8f315bb8` extends the bounded whole-body static
integer-state analysis to readonly native reference fields of formal receivers.
Owned primitive array headers are authenticated with the tracked field shape.
Their SSA metadata follows the actual captured array, while integer cell values
can remain in invocation locals between immediate canonical stores. Meaningful
handlers, volatile fields, instance writes, unsupported effects and unproved
array origins still reject this proof. Existing loop/inline recovery remains
responsible for fuel and exact Java continuations; no new runtime flag exists.

A final `aaload` is admitted only as the last instruction directly returned by
that block. It may call a foreign getter after the reader has committed all its
writes, but cannot return to the certified body. Such methods **never publish a
closed native contract or trusted closed export**. A reference read followed by
more Java effects remains outside this proof.

Tests expose two important distinctions. A captured-array loop may no longer
need its original receiver local after a fuel exit. Requiring that dead receiver
again causes an unnecessary fallback. The compiler now computes reachability
from the supported resume header: receivers/field headers needed only by the
skipped prefix are not demanded on resumed entry, and the restored original
array is authenticated directly. This does not substitute the receiver's new
field value for the captured array. A second test exposes a pre-existing generic
foreign-array fallback bug: a getter writes a static cell to 6, but a later Java
increment uses the cached 1 and stores 2. The foreign reference-array branch now
invalidates field/object caches before invoking the getter; the test obtains 7.
The owned GC-array branch retains its fast path.

The new fixture also validates cold initialization after the original prefix,
actual scalar/atomic-leaf inlining, vector identity, terminal getter side effects
and throwable identity, original outer bounds handlers, private field shadows,
volatile rejection, resumed ownership, prefix non-replay and zero late Java
compilation. The raw reference-return export propagates a host throwable directly;
the fixture checks its exact identity rather than imposing a scalar-export status
convention. Its initial handler wrapper returned a reference, which the existing
partial-module policy does not support; an integer sentinel wrapper tests the
same original exception behavior without requiring a new compiler policy.

### Revoked private wrapper bindings, and excluded array regions

Experimental JVM source `ef7a951eafd6b3670951e17be63cbcd3ef9c6ba4` keeps
tracked Java wrappers behind a shared proxy. Its private binding flag is revoked

revocation. Binding certificates remain per wrapper, while shape certification
is shared by wrappers of the same field container. Revalidating one container
cannot revive another wrapper's invalid binding. GC storage layout and lifetime
are unchanged. This is a JavaScript private certificate, not a new Wasm GC ABI.

### Private returned-array ownership: useful small-case proof, no loading gain yet

The previous array-region failure motivates a precise handoff question: numeric
base/length transport already supports unregistered host aliases, so it cannot
by itself certify ownership. Experimental source
`3aaf977c84575b60c497aad9a5285e8e00cdc529` adds a separate private `owned` global
to per-method array-return transport. Private field/element headers can establish
it; plain parameter/generic metadata cannot. A caller captures/drains all three
words immediately around its canonical call, and unknown/withdrawn JavaScript
bridges clear them after any nested native invocation. Only positive private
metadata seeds the regional source cache. It is marked authenticated before
first use, so entry into the region does not discard a just-produced proof.
SSA redefinition, invocation and resumption keep their existing revocation rules.
The certificate supplies location/length, not a cast or bulk-copy kind verdict.

### Compiler-paired native storage with synchronous revocation

The controlled trusted-entry bound justified a real generic ownership mechanism,
not transporting its fixture assumption into the runtime. Source
`5c2f85dc306a0787e5868ccd64fe39e69c72508b` adds a monotonic i32 certificate to
private GC field storage: 0 is unissued, 1 is valid, -1 is permanently revoked.
Tracked wrapper-binding and field-shape edits revoke before performing the edit;
aliases share the certificate. Java field writes retain it. Checked descriptor
validation may recover a valid alias, but cannot reissue the native certificate.
Manual registrations and raw stores do not earn pairing. Class identity remains
a separate immutable field. Ordinary and paired entry modes are distinct from
the existing callback-free closed-body contract.

Source `6b2d4f799cb2051a5dbbfbb7cfcdbe237e19dd3b` connects that mechanism to actual
compiled calls. Only a bounded whole stateful body whose required receivers are
native object parameters publishes the paired-entry contract. A caller proves
the relationship to its actual Java SSA receiver using a WeakMap-only tracked
lookup, independently of its incoming transport payload. Its separate captured
store survives opaque calls while its native certificate remains valid; redefining
that SSA receiver clears it. The actual GC argument placed on the operand stack
is checked before choosing the paired slot. The callee checks revocation again,
so even a callback after slot selection cannot use an expired proof. Null,
foreign and modified receivers retain checked entry and precise continuation.

Pairing has its own slot and method/signature/proof identity. Replacement without
the proof publishes the compatible ordinary entry; withdrawal keeps the existing
bridge, and caller retirement releases the extra slot. Publication never treats
this entry-only contract as a callback-free method. The duplicate-code budget is
shared with existing entries, whose emission choices remain first. Installed
metadata contains plain contracts, not SSA graphs.

Focused validation exposed a new fallback map retaining SSA call keys; adding
both new discovery maps to compiler cleanup fixes the weak-reference test. A
first late-mutation test incorrectly expected a normal raw return: replacement
correctly refuses native ownership and hands off. The corrected test follows the
